content:
henry: FYI customer complaining about streaming endpoints tail latency (p95/p99). They say TTFB spikes to 6-12s intermittently, but if they switch to non-streaming the tail goes away. Request IDs: rq_01G8X2PJ..., sample tenant: cust-47.

henry: Customer example repro (they used internal SDK but this is a curl repro):
```bash
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \\n  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  --http2 \\n  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate/stream \\n  -d '{"model":"rwd-base-1","input":"short prompt","stream":true}'
```

mira: thanks. two quick hypotheses: 1) upstream proxy/buffer (nginx/ALB/cloudflare) is coalescing chunks -> delays TTFB, 2) server-side flush interval or SDK flush buffer is too large so first chunk is delayed.

ryan: +1. Also watch for HTTP/2 and proxy buffering interplay. Many proxies buffer until a minimum amount or timeout. Need headers like `X-Accel-Buffering: no` and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and proxy config `proxy_buffering off` for nginx.

henry: customer says they run behind Cloudflare + corporate proxy. They also see intermittent 502s in the same window but most are 200s after delay.

henry: paste of our streaming handler logs around one of the slow TTFB events:
```
[2026-03-14T14:12:41.123Z] stream.start rq=rq_01G8X2PJ tenant=cust-47 model=rwd-base-1
[2026-03-14T14:12:41.130Z] kernel.select kernels=matmul_fast seq=64
[2026-03-14T14:12:41.220Z] kvcache.warm start
[2026-03-14T14:12:41.420Z] stream.flush scheduled interval_ms=1000
[2026-03-14T14:12:47.432Z] stream.chunk sent size=8192
```
Notice flush interval is 1000ms and first actual network chunk leaves ~6s later (due to buffering upstream).

mira: ran an internal repro from our EU egress (no Cloudflare) and got: p50=110ms, p95=2.1s, p99=6.3s for streaming. Non-streaming p99=1.4s. So server side contributes but upstream amplifies it. I can reproduce slower tails when going through a proxy that enables buffering.

ryan: can we check edge headers for `Via`, `X-Accel-Buffering` or `X-Proxy-Buffered`? Also see if `Content-Length` ever set by mistake (should be chunked).

henry: customer provided a raw response header snapshot. It includes `Server: cloudflare`, and a custom header `X-Proxy-Buffered: 1`.

natasha: SDK note: older JS SDK versions batched small writes into a single flush by default. Which SDK is the customer using? If they're on <=0.9.x we had a bug where autoFlush defaulted to 1s. Recommend forcing flushIntervalMs=200 in the SDK as a temp workaround.

henry: customer is on JS SDK 0.9.1. They can try non-streaming but prefer streaming for UX.

mira: proposed immediate triage plan:
- confirm reproduction via `curl -N` from multiple networks (internal, customer).
- ask infra to canary disable proxy buffering for streaming route and set `proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_buffering off; proxy_buffers 4 1k; proxy_busy_buffers_size 1k;`
- lower runtime flush interval to 200-250ms for streaming endpoints (server-side config)
- request customer to try SDK override `flushIntervalMs=200` or use non-streaming while we canary.

ryan: I'll prepare an ingress patch for the streaming route and schedule a canary in eu-west-1. Note: nginx config change may impact memory so we'll restrict to the specific path and to a single canary shard.

mira: quick repro command I used (internal) to simulate proxy buffering behavior:
```bash
# simulate proxy that buffers until 8k or 3s
python3 tests/proxy_sim.py --buffer-threshold 8192 --timeout 3 &
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \\n  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \\n  --http1.1 http://127.0.0.1:8080/stream -d '{"model":"rwd-base-1","stream":true}'
```
It reproduces p99 ~5-7s depending on buffer/timeout.

henry: customer asked for temporary workaround we can recommend now. I'll send: 1) toggle stream=false (non-streaming) 2) If they need streaming, ask them to disable their proxy buffering for the route or enable Cloudflare 'response streaming' option (if available) 3) override SDK flushIntervalMs=200.

natasha: I'll open RNW-1234 and add runbook steps + customer comms template. Runbook checklist: how to repro, how to toggle canary, rollback steps, monitoring queries, and follow-up SDK release note.

ryan: longer-term items (post-mortem candidates):
- make server default flushInterval 250ms for streaming models serving short prompts 
- add backpressure metric for server chunk queue and an alert when queue latency >500ms
- improve docs for streaming caveats behind proxies (Cloudflare, corp proxies, ALB)

infra-bot: canary deploy scheduled: https://deploys.redwood.internal/deploys/7891 (target: streaming-route eu-west-1, start: 2026-03-14T16:00Z).

mira: action items / owners / ETA: 
- ryan: ingress canary patch (nginx proxy_buffering off) -> canary 16:00Z today.
- ryan: update ingress template for targeted route after canary success -> ETA 48h.
- infra-bot: create alert p95_streaming_latency > 2s -> done (RNW-1234).
- natasha: RNW-1234 + customer comms + runbook -> first draft 2h.
- henry: send customer workaround + repro steps, ask for cloudflare proxy settings info -> now.
- mira: follow up with metrics after canary -> 30m after canary.

henry: I'll message the customer with the workaround and update this thread when they respond. Thanks all. :thumbsup:"
